encounters.cc: Interested in enrolling in a clinical research study for cardiovascular risk reduction.

lines: Interested in enrolling in a clinical research study for cardiovascular risk reduction.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks monthly).
She is enrolled in a randomized controlled trial comparing a new lipid-lowering agent to standard statin therapy.
The primary outcome is a reduction in LDL cholesterol by at least 30 mg/dL after 12 weeks.
The investigators expect a moderate effect size and set the significance level (alpha) at 0.05.
Due to constraints in recruitment, only 60 patients are enrolled in each arm of the study.
At the conclusion, the mean LDL reduction in the experimental group is 32 mg/dL, and in the control group, it is 27 mg/dL, with a calculated p-value of 0.08.
The investigators note that, given the sample size and expected effect, the study had a calculated power of 65%.

lines: Persistent dry cough for the past 2 months after starting new blood pressure medication.

She has a history of hypertension.

Her other medications include atorvastatin and a daily aspirin.

The rest of the examination is unremarkable.

lines: Six-month history of difficult-to-control hypertension despite adherence to triple therapy.

Despite adherence to metoprolol, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide, blood pressure remains elevated at 162/98 mmHg.
She takes metoprolol, amlodipine, and hydrochlorothiazide.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)

encounters.cc: Enrolling in randomized controlled trial comparing new lipid-lowering agent with standard statin therapy.

lines: Enrolling in randomized controlled trial comparing new lipid-lowering agent with standard statin therapy.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks monthly).
The investigators wish to detect a true difference in mean LDL reduction of at least 18 mg/dL, with a standard deviation of 20 mg/dL in both groups.
They set the significance level (α) at 0.05 and calculate that a sample size of 50 per group provides a study power of 70%.
After analyzing the results, the p-value is found to be 0.11, and the null hypothesis is not rejected.
The researchers are concerned about the possibility of a type II (β) error.

encounters.cc: Routine research follow-up visit for clinical trial participation and study methodology review.

lines: Routine research follow-up visit for clinical trial participation and study methodology review.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks monthly).
Participates in a randomized controlled trial assessing the effect of a new antihypertensive drug versus placebo.
The investigators predefine the significance level (alpha) at 0.01 instead of the more common 0.05 due to concerns about multiple comparisons and the risk of type I errors.
The trial enrolls 150 patients in each arm and observes a mean systolic blood pressure reduction of 7 mmHg (p = 0.03) in the treatment group compared to placebo.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and hand tremors with confusion and difficulty walking.

lines: Two-day history of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and hand tremors with confusion and difficulty walking.
This 58-year-old female with bipolar I disorder, hypertension, and renal artery stenosis presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and hand tremors.
She reports that she has been feeling increasingly confused and has had difficulty walking due to a sense of imbalance.
Her medical history is significant for hypertension.
She takes stabilized on lithium. she recently started taking a new medication, but she cannot recall its name.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks monthly).
Her vital signs are within normal limits.
Physical examination reveals mild ataxia and a fine tremor in both hands.

lines: Recurrent episodes of acute shortness of breath at night relieved by sitting upright, following recent hospitalization for flash pulmonary edema.
The patient with a history of renal artery stenosis returns with recurrent episodes of acute shortness of breath at night that awakens her from sleep.
She reports that these episodes are relieved by sitting upright.
She also mentions a recent episode of flash pulmonary edema that required hospitalization.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks monthly).
A bruit is audible over the right upper quadrant of the abdomen
A Doppler ultrasound of the renal arteries shows a significant stenosis of the right renal artery.

encounters.cc: Severe worsening nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hand tremors, confusion, and unsteady gait progressing over 2 days.

lines: Severe worsening nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, hand tremors, confusion, and unsteady gait progressing over 2 days.
The patient is a 59-year-old female with Bipolar I Disorder on chronic lithium therapy and a history of prior lithium toxicity in March 2022 who presents with recurrence of similar symptoms.
She reports a 2-day history of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and hand tremors.
She reports feeling "confused and unsteady" when walking.
She denies any recent illness, travel, or changes in her diet.
- Secondary hypertension due to renal artery stenosis (diagnosed 2022-09-15)
She takes lithium, hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension, and sertraline for depression.
- Brother: Premature coronary artery disease (MI at age 52)
Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 drinks monthly).
Blood pressure 130/85 mmHg, heart rate 92 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F)
On physical examination, she is alert but appears distressed.
Neurological examination reveals mild ataxia and a fine tremor in both hands.
